$why: PER-TASK MODEL ROUTING — the single place that says which model does which
kind of work. §2.4 of docs/twinai-master-build-plan.md.
THIS DOES NOT INTRODUCE ROUTING. Routing already existed, decided three
separate ways and written down nowhere:
DIRECTOR_MODEL      a frozen constant in directorContract.ts, deliberately
never read from env, recorded in the decision row and
the analyzer bundle
env.fastModel       an env knob passed at exactly ONE call site
(structure.ts), whose own comment gives a task-class
argument: 'MECHANICAL ... schema-constrained tasks'
the geminiJson      an implicit fallthrough to GEMINI_MODEL for everything
default             that passed no model at all
Three mechanisms, two different default models, and nothing comparing them.
That is the same shape as the twelve analysis-component allowlists removed
in #244 — a decision made in several places that no one place records.
SO THIS FILE ENCODES WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE. Every entry below is the model
that task uses TODAY. Landing it changes no model for any task, which is
the only safe way to introduce an authority over live behaviour — the same
property that made wiring `pacing` safe: the default path returns exactly
what it returned before.
WHY TASK CLASS AND NOT CALL SITE. A call site is where the twelve-allowlist
defect comes from: a dozen places each privately encoding a choice, none
referencing any other. A task class is the granularity the work actually
has — extracting structured evidence, choosing among candidates, and writing
prose differ in cost, in latency, and in what a wrong answer costs.
PROVENANCE IS THE NON-NEGOTIABLE. Which model produced an artefact must stay
recoverable. `envOverride: null` means the model is FROZEN and cannot be
changed by configuration — that is what makes the Director's decision
reproducible from its recorded bundle, and it must stay null.
$taskClasses: decide        choose among candidates against evidence; the answer is a
structured decision somebody will be held to
extract       pull structured facts out of a document under a fixed schema;
mechanical, and the schema does the constraining
profile       infer and write prose about a brand or voice; open-ended, and
the cost of a mediocre answer is a worse script
$THE_ROUTING_LOOKS_INVERTED: RECORDED ON THE DAY THIS CATALOG WAS BUILT, because writing the three
choices next to each other for the first time made it visible. It is a
FINDING, not a change: nothing here has been re-pointed.
decide   the Director -- picks cuts, hook, pacing, captions and zooms
from evidence, at temperature 0.2, and every video is shaped by
it                                        -> FLASH
extract  schema-constrained reference extraction, whose own env comment
argued a flash model costs 'no quality loss on these
schema-constrained tasks'                 -> PRO
The hardest judgement runs on the cheap model; the most mechanical task
pays the premium its own documentation said it did not need. Nobody chose
that. It is what three independent decisions add up to: the Director was
pinned to flash, GEMINI_FAST_MODEL was never set so extraction fell back to
the expensive default, and profile reached its model by passing nothing.
WHY THIS IS NOT FIXED HERE. Re-pointing `decide` changes what the model
sees and therefore what it produces, and this project has a director-eval
harness and a quality gate precisely because that is not a judgement to
make by reasoning. Changing `extract` is cheaper to justify -- the argument
is already written in the code -- but it is still a live behaviour change
and belongs in its own reviewable step, measured rather than assumed.
So this catalog LANDS AS A NO-OP and makes the question askable. The next
move is an eval, not an edit. Naming replacement model ids from memory
would be the same chosen-not-measured mistake this repo has already made
three times over -- a 50-minute CI cap against a real 77, a 25% hook-trim
threshold against a legitimate 28.7% case, and an 80 ms caption tail guard
against a real 93-120 ms shortfall.
